classification.difficultyReason: Apply the definition of a diagonal to supplied figures, including recognising when no diagonal exists.

inlines.text: Draw all diagonals of each polygon. If a shape has no diagonals, state this.

spec.mathematics: Four vertices; diagonals connect opposite vertices.

answer.worked: Join each pair of opposite vertices. There are 2 diagonals.

spec.mathematics: The two opposite-vertex pairs are joined.
spec.answerVisibility: Completed diagonals appear only in the answer.

spec.description: Landscape parallelogram with horizontal parallel sides and sides rising to the right.

answer.worked: Join each pair of opposite vertices. There are 2 diagonals.

spec.mathematics: Both pairs of opposite vertices joined.

spec.description: Square rotated into a diamond orientation.
spec.mathematics: Top, right, bottom and left vertices; no labels.

answer.worked: Join the top vertex to the bottom vertex and the left vertex to the right vertex. There are 2 diagonals.

spec.description: Diamond-oriented square with horizontal and vertical diagonals.
Trapezium with a shorter horizontal top side and longer horizontal base.

answer.worked: Join each top vertex to the opposite bottom vertex. There are 2 diagonals.

spec.description: Convex hexagon with horizontal top and bottom sides.
spec.mathematics: Six vertices; each has three non-adjacent vertices.

answer.worked: Join every pair of non-adjacent vertices, drawing each segment once. The completed hexagon has 9 diagonals.

spec.mathematics: All nine unordered non-adjacent vertex pairs are joined once.

answer.worked: Join the left vertex to the right vertex and the upper vertex to the lower vertex. There are 2 diagonals.

spec.description: Convex heptagon with an uppermost vertex and horizontal bottom side.
spec.mathematics: Seven vertices; each has four non-adjacent vertices.

answer.worked: Join every pair of non-adjacent vertices, drawing each segment once. The completed heptagon has 14 diagonals.

spec.mathematics: All fourteen unordered non-adjacent vertex pairs are joined once.
Every pair of vertices is adjacent, so no diagonal exists.

answer.short: No diagonals: every pair of vertices is adjacent.
answer.worked: A diagonal joins non-adjacent vertices. Every pair of vertices in a triangle is adjacent, so the triangle has no diagonals.

spec.description: Unlabelled circle with no marked points or internal segments.
spec.mathematics: A circle is not a polygon and has no vertices or diagonals.

answer.short: No diagonals: a circle has no vertices.
answer.worked: A diagonal joins two non-adjacent vertices of a polygon. A circle is not a polygon and has no vertices, so it has no diagonals.
